$comment: THE SHARED FIXTURE — docs/PRODUCT_v0.3.md §5.2, 'the honest residual, not buried'.
C20 moved the derived-state arithmetic to the server, so it now exists TWICE: in Kotlin
(domain/model/User.kt — Leveling, and the client's own reading of a fact set) and in
TypeScript (functions/src/projection.ts). That is a second IMPLEMENTATION, and two
implementations of one rule can disagree. §5.2 accepted the duplication — avoiding it costs
the offline win entirely — on one condition: that both are pinned by ONE fixture both test
This is that file. It is NOT two copies of the same numbers; it is one copy read from two
Both resolve it by walking up from their own module directory, so neither owns it.
ADDING A CASE IS THE POINT. A number that disagreed in the wild belongs here as a case,
not as a fix in one language. If you change the level curve or the points rule, change it
here first and let both suites go red.
SHAPE. Every case gives the FACTS and the EXPECTED PROJECTION. Facts are what the user did;
the projection is what the server stores. Nothing here stores a level: publicProfiles.level
was deleted by C20 (a stored function of points in the same document), so `level` below is
asserted as a COMPUTED value on both sides and never as a written field.

pointsCases.name: tasks exist but none are done — an undone task contributes nothing
only the done ones are summed
exactly on a level boundary — L2 begins at 100, inclusive
one point below a boundary stays on the lower level
L4 begins at 600, and a big pile does not skip past it
a negative task value cannot drag the total below zero
a task with no points field counts as zero, not as a crash
idempotence, stated as data — the same fact set always gives the same number
$note: Two ROWS with the same id cannot exist in Firestore, so this case does not model a
duplicate document. It models the only way projection could double-credit — two facts
of equal weight — and pins that the answer is arithmetic over whatever the fact set
holds, never an accumulator. Run the projection twice on the real set and you get 240
both times; that is what 'structurally idempotent' means and why FieldValue.increment

scoreCases.name: a report of zero is a report, not an absence
the latest absolute report is the score — the UI reports a total, not a delta
a negative report is clamped rather than stored
no report at all leaves the row alone
$note: score: null means DO NOT WRITE. Deleting the report fact (leaving the challenge, or an
undo) must not silently zero a standing other people are reading — the projection
writes nothing and the last reported number stands until the row itself is deleted.
